resource.name: aws_efs_mount_target
resource.description: Provides an Elastic File System (EFS) mount target.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_efs_mount_target` resource enables the creation and management of mount targets for Amazon Elastic File System (EFS), allowing instances within a VPC to access shared file storage. It is commonly used to configure high-availability, scalable storage solutions for applications, data processing workflows, or containerized environments. Key configurations include specifying subnet associations, security groups for access control, and lifecycle management to ensure reliable connectivity and performance across multiple availability zones.

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_efs_mount_target` resource to attach an EFS file system to a specific subnet within a VPC. It showcases the use of key arguments like `file_system_id` and `subnet_id`, along with the creation of supporting resources (`aws_vpc` and `aws_subnet`) to establish the necessary network infrastructure for the mount target.

arguments.name: file_system_id
arguments.description: (Required) The ID of the file system for which the mount target is intended.
arguments.llm_summary: The `file_system_id` argument specifies the unique identifier of the Amazon EFS file system to which the mount target will connect, enabling the user to associate the mount target with a specific file system for network access. By defining this required parameter, users ensure the mount target is correctly linked to the desired EFS resource, facilitating storage access and integration within their cloud infrastructure.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument in the `aws_efs_mount_target` resource represents the unique identifier of the mount target, typically auto-generated by AWS upon creation. While not required to be explicitly set by the user, it serves as a reference for identifying and managing the mount target in Terraform configurations or external integrations, supporting tasks like resource tracking and dependency management.

arguments.name: ip_address
arguments.description: (Optional) The address (within the address range of the specified subnet) at which the file system may be mounted via the mount target.
arguments.llm_summary: The `ip_address` argument for the `aws_efs_mount_target` resource allows users to specify a custom IP address within the subnet's CIDR range for the mount target, enabling precise control over the network configuration of the EFS mount point. This is useful for scenarios requiring predictable or static IP assignments for integration with other networked resources or applications.

arguments.name: security_groups
arguments.description: (Optional) A list of up to 5 VPC security group IDs (that must be for the same VPC as subnet specified) in effect for the mount target.
arguments.llm_summary: The `security_groups` argument for the `aws_efs_mount_target` resource allows users to specify up to 5 VPC security group IDs to control network-level access to the mount target. By configuring this argument, users can define inbound and outbound traffic rules, ensuring secure connectivity and access management for the associated EFS file system within the specified VPC subnet.

arguments.name: subnet_id
arguments.description: (Required) The ID of the subnet to add the mount target in.
arguments.llm_summary: The `subnet_id` argument specifies the ID of the subnet in which the Amazon EFS mount target will be created, allowing users to control the network placement and connectivity of the mount target within a specific VPC. By defining this argument, users ensure the mount target is accessible within the designated subnet, aligning with their network architecture and enabling secure access to the EFS file system from resources in that subnet.

blocks.name: timeouts

arguments.name: create
arguments.llm_summary: The `create` argument within the `timeouts` block of the `aws_efs_mount_target` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (in string format, e.g., "10m") Terraform will wait for the creation of an EFS mount target to complete. Configuring this timeout ensures better control over resource provisioning, particularly in environments where network or service delays may impact the creation process.

arguments.name: delete
arguments.llm_summary: The `delete` argument within the `timeouts` block for the `aws_efs_mount_target` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (as a string) Terraform should wait for the deletion of an EFS mount target to complete. By configuring this timeout, users can control the resource lifecycle behavior, ensuring operations do not hang indefinitely or fail prematurely during the deletion process.

blocks.llm_summary: The `timeouts` configuration block in the `aws_efs_mount_target` resource allows users to define custom timeout durations for specific lifecycle operations, such as creating, updating, or deleting an EFS mount target. By configuring this block, users gain precise control over operation time limits, ensuring smoother management of resource provisioning and avoiding potential timeout errors in complex or slow network environments.

attributes.name: availability_zone_id
attributes.description: The unique and consistent identifier of the Availability Zone (AZ) that the mount target resides in.

attributes.name: availability_zone_name
attributes.description: The name of the Availability Zone (AZ) that the mount target resides in.

attributes.name: dns_name
attributes.description: The DNS name for the EFS file system.

attributes.name: file_system_arn
attributes.description: Amazon Resource Name of the file system.

attributes.name: mount_target_dns_name
attributes.description: The DNS name for the given subnet/AZ per documented convention.

attributes.name: network_interface_id
attributes.description: The ID of the network interface that Amazon EFS created when it created the mount target.

attributes.name: owner_id
attributes.description: AWS account ID that owns the resource.
